title: Suspicious Bank Verification
summary: A retiree receives an urgent message about an account flag and a possible transfer hold.

context.objective: Find evidence that supports fake account verification, urgent transfer pressure, or impersonation.
context.question: Which clue best supports the bank verification scam?
context.hint: Look for language that sounds official but pushes the victim to act quickly.
context.warning: Irrelevant details will waste time and weaken the investigation.

evidence.text: Caller claims the bank detected a suspicious login and asks for verification.
evidence.assessment: Directly supports the scam pattern because it uses fake account verification pressure.
evidence.hint: This sounds like the core bank-impersonation lead.

evidence.text: Text includes a fake bank link and a warning about account suspension.
evidence.assessment: Very useful because the fake link and threat language confirm a phishing-style setup.
evidence.hint: The link and warning language are strong signs of fraud.

evidence.text: A family member noticed the same number used in another scam report.
evidence.assessment: Helpful as supporting evidence, but it needs other clues to confirm the pattern.
evidence.hint: This clue supports the case, but it does not explain the scam by itself.

evidence.text: Bank security notice mentions unusual transfer pressure and urgent language.
evidence.assessment: Strong investigative clue because it matches common fraud escalation language.
evidence.hint: This is a good match for the current bank-pressure theory.

evidence.text: The victim also mentions that the internet was slow earlier in the day.
evidence.assessment: Not very useful because it does not connect directly to the scam behavior.
evidence.hint: This detail is probably a distraction unless another clue proves otherwise.
